title: Eyes Only
pitch: Each plate is a mosaic of colored dots hiding a creature or a letter, and each of five simulated eyes (typical, protan, deutan, tritan, achromat) reads a different part of the picture. The visitor flips lenses, with a severity dial for milder forms, to see what each eye reveals, decodes cipher words whose letters need different eyes, and builds plates in a studio where a solver tunes the dots until exactly the chosen eyes can read them. A real lab result, dichromats out-spotting trichromats on color-camouflaged texture, inspires the masked plates, so the eye most often called deficient is the one that cracks the code.
whyNow: Timeless. About 1 in 12 men have a color vision deficiency (as of 2026-10-11, per NEI), and the science behind the plates (camouflage-breaking studies, a 2009 simulation model) is stable and citable.

research.summary: A 1992 study reported that dichromats beat trichromats at finding texture-defined targets hidden by random red-green coloring, and a later review states dichromats do better when color is irrelevant to the task; early stimuli were stylized, so the effect is real but task-dependent. A 2009 IEEE TVCG paper by Machado, Oliveira and Fernandes gives a physiologically based simulation model covering dichromacy and anomalous trichromacy. About 1 in 12 men have a color vision deficiency (NEI), and deuteranomaly, a milder form, is the most common type, which motivates a severity dial. A cone-opponent view (luminance, red-green, blue-yellow) explains what each lens keeps; one paper cautions that some dichromats keep residual red-green discrimination. The design splits plates into exact ones (pure channel signals that vanish after the lens by construction) and perceptual ones (masking, labeled as a model).

sources.title: Dichromats detect colour-camouflaged objects that are not detected by trichromats
sources.snippet: PubMed record of Morgan, Adam and Mollon (Proc. R. Soc. B). Per the search summary, random red-green coloring of texture elements made the target harder for trichromats but not for dichromats, who did better.
sources.note: The core finding that inspires the masked plates. Not opened; the title states the finding and a later review agrees. Year 1992 comes from the search summary.

sources.title: Relative advantages of dichromatic and trichromatic color vision in camouflage breaking
sources.snippet: Review article. The search summary says it reports dichromats outperforming trichromats at finding camouflaged targets when color is irrelevant to the task, and that early stimuli were stylized shapes with extreme colors.
sources.note: Independent review supporting the finding and its limits (stylized stimuli); the limit goes into the risks.

sources.title: A physiologically-based model for simulation of color vision deficiency
sources.snippet: University repository record of the Machado, Oliveira and Fernandes paper (IEEE TVCG 15(6), 1291-1298). Per the abstract in the search summary, one model handles normal vision, anomalous trichromacy and dichromacy.
sources.note: The simulation model behind the lens engine. The abstract was seen only through a search summary.

sources.title: Color Blindness
sources.snippet: National Eye Institute overview page. Per the search summary, its fact box says about 1 in 12 men have color vision deficiency, and women are less often affected because the common genes are X-linked.
sources.note: Headline prevalence, attributed explicitly to NEI in the summary. Not opened.

sources.title: About Colour Blindness - Colour Blind Awareness
sources.snippet: Colour Blind Awareness page. Per the search summary, sources commonly give about 1 in 12 men (8 percent) and 1 in 200 women; that summary blended several results.
sources.note: Second organization for the prevalence figure (blended summary, but the title matches the topic).

sources.title: Types of Color Vision Deficiency - National Eye Institute - NIH
sources.snippet: NEI page grouping deuteranomaly (the most common red-green type), protanomaly, protanopia and deuteranopia; blue-yellow forms are less common and complete color blindness is rare.
sources.note: Names the lens types and shows that milder anomalous forms dominate, which motivates the severity dial.

sources.title: The evolution of concepts of color vision - PMC
sources.snippet: Review. The search summary says only a fraction of color-defective males are true dichromats (roughly 1 percent protanopes and 2 percent deuteranopes) and partial forms are much more common.
sources.note: Independent review agreeing that milder forms dominate.

sources.title: Curing Color Blindness-Mice and Nonhuman Primates - PMC
sources.snippet: Review. Per the search summary, dichromats keep blue-yellow and black-white percepts and achromatic channels that carry brightness, but lack the normal sensations of red and green.
sources.note: Supports the lens-channel model: luminance and blue-yellow survive for red-green dichromats.

sources.title: Why do Protan & Deutan look so similar?
sources.snippet: Blog post. Per the search summary, luminance is the sum of the cone signals and the red-green channel compares red and green cone signals, so losing either cone type removes the red-green channel.
sources.note: Secondary explanatory source agreeing with the review on the channel structure; a blog, so weighted lightly.

sources.title: escholarship.org (UC eScholarship PDF; result title shown as 'escholarship.org')
sources.snippet: Per the search summary, a paper reports protanopes and deuteranopes are believed unable to make small-field red-versus-green judgments but argues some residual red-green discrimination may exist.
sources.note: Single-source caveat that the complete-loss view is contested; kept as a risk, not as a page fact.

facts.claim: Morgan, Adam and Mollon (Proc. R. Soc. B, 1992) reported that dichromats detected color-camouflaged texture targets that trichromats found harder, because random color interferes with texture-based segregation; a later review reports dichromats outperform trichromats when color is irrelevant to the task.

Machado, Oliveira and Fernandes published a physiologically based color vision deficiency simulation model in IEEE TVCG 15(6), 1291-1298 (2009); the abstract, seen through a search summary, says it covers normal vision, anomalous trichromacy and dichromacy.
About 1 in 12 men have a color vision deficiency, and women are far less often affected (NEI; Colour Blind Awareness).
Deuteranomaly, a milder anomalous form of red-green deficiency, is the most common type, and partial forms are more common than true dichromacy.
Red-green dichromats lose the red-green opponent signal but keep luminance (achromatic) and blue-yellow signals.
As of 2026-10-11, per a UC eScholarship paper (one source, unverified), some protanopes and deuteranopes may keep residual red-green discrimination, so a channel model is a simplification.

design.coreLoop: A seeded plate packs about two thousand dots of mixed radii; a hidden figure is encoded as a small offset in chosen cone-contrast directions (L, M, S or luminance) with masking noise in others. The visitor switches among five lenses (keys 1 to 5) or drags a severity dial, moves a reticle to the figure, and receives a per-lens detectability readout plus a reveal card explaining which eyes could read the plate and why. Cipher mode spreads a word over plates, one letter per subset of eyes. Studio mode takes a target set of readers and runs a solver that tunes channel amplitudes and noise until the model's detectability meets the target, or reports the target infeasible. A map of all 32 reader subsets fills in as plates are made, with unreachable cells greyed out, which gives a collection goal for the tenth minute.
sophisticationHooks: Lens engine: 3x3 linear-RGB simulation matrices in the Machado style with a severity dial from typical to full dichromacy (anomalous trichromacy included), an achromat luminance lens, and self-tests (neutral gray unchanged; red-green pairs collapse under deutan and protan; blue-yellow pairs collapse under tritan).

Plate generator: seeded blue-noise circle packing with mixed radii on a spatial hash grid, figure masks from signed-distance creature shapes and a 5x7 glyph set, dot colors sampled in a cone-contrast space with gamut-safe scaling, fully deterministic from the URL hash.

Detectability model: a d-prime style score per lens (figure versus ground difference over pooled noise in the channels the lens still has) plus a clutter term where chromatic noise masks luminance signals for lenses that still see it, the Morgan-style effect; exact plates (pure channel signals) are separated from perceptual plates (masking) and labeled.

Studio solver and feasibility map: coordinate-descent search with restarts over signal mix, amplitude and per-channel noise to hit any of the 32 reader subsets; subsets that violate the channel structure are shown infeasible under the model and greyed in the map.
design.scopeForOneDay: Built: lens engine and self-tests (about 250 lines), generator and renderer (about 300), detectability model and solver (about 250), UI for Hunt, Cipher and Studio modes with keyboard reticle and touch, severity dial, reveal cards, 12 specimen shapes and the glyph set, 40 curated seeds, URL-hash sharing, about and making-of panel listing verified sources only. Cut if short: sonified plate (pitch from local detectability), image import, palette tool, per-lens custom mixing.
risks: Perceptual claims: whether a typical eye misses a masked plate depends on the person and the display; the page grades by the model and labels those plates perceptual, while exact plates are true by construction.
The page is a puzzle and a model, not a vision test or diagnosis; the copy avoids telling any visitor what their own vision is.

Simulation caveats: disability-simulation critiques, residual red-green discrimination reported for some dichromats (one source, unverified), and varied displays; the about panel states them and shows the residual-discrimination point as 'as of 2026-10-11, per UC eScholarship'.

The camouflage advantage is documented for stylized stimuli and specific tasks (per a review in the search results), so the copy states it as a lab result and makes no general claim about colorblind people.
Matrix constants have to be reproduced from the published model without opening it; the fallback derives lenses from an LMS projection and the self-tests check neutrals and confusion-pair collapse.
A visual puzzle is not fully playable by blind visitors; text reveal cards and the optional sonified plate (cut if short) are the mitigation.
